### Preservation mode: an MRC document beside the e-ink preparation mode

`active` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.preservation-mode/2`

Preserve is the second top-level mode beside e-ink Preparation, shipped in the CLI (--preserve) and the liminalUI GUI (Preparation | Preserve): page colour is retained, PDF as a JPEG 2000 background under crisp JBIG2 ink, DjVu as IW44 plus JB2, at the requested resolution; hOCR stays independent and TrueTyping is explicit opt-in. What remains is verification and fidelity: decode and look at DjVu output, a three-book size and time table, the pre-refactor grayscale identity gate, and the deferred fidelity items (coloured ink, which is black in this cut; colour on the source-MRC passthrough; supersampled coverage).

### Measure jp2lam photographic quality per byte against JPEG XL and BPG after the SSIMULACRA2 controller

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.improve-photographic-rate-control/1`

### jp2lam decoder optimisation: the remaining tail

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.jp2lam-jpeg-2000-decoder-optimization-plan/1`

The single live record for the jp2lam JPEG 2000 decoder optimisation effort; the codec now lives at exprim/codecs/jp2lam (moved 2026-11-09; jp2lam 0.4.0 released 2026-11-24). The detailed authority is still the five decode-fix-plan documents beside it. Re-verified 2026-11-27 against jp2lam 0.4.0: of the seven items open on 2026-09-08, the Tier-2 cleanups (no merged-block hash map, lazy PacketProgression), packed stripe flags with the branch-light MQ decoder and AVX2 kernels, the sYCC kernel for any equal chroma subsampling, and tile-part QCC/QCD/COC overrides have landed.
What remains, all profiling-gated or demand-gated: (1) a windowed, line-based inverse DWT for region decode (today only intersecting code blocks are decoded and the IDWT still runs whole per tile; chroma-subsampled region decode is refused); (2) PGO and further SIMD or GPU experiments, after refreshing stage attribution with the current decode benchmark; (3) wiring Rgbx8/Bgra8 decode output through exprim's src/image/jpx.rs once a BGRA or GPU upload consumer exists; (4) POC, PPM, PPT and RGN marker support only if the census finds files that need them. Negative result kept: the wide f32x8 fused ICT/clamp/interleave experiment (c2c8dbf1) was neutral because the stage is bandwidth-bound.

### Train an own page-dewarp model on Colab that beats Paddle UVDoc, flattener and DocScanner on book spreads and leaves flat pages alone

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.own-page-dewarp-model/2`

Train from ImageNet-initialised ResNet-18 trunk + three transformer layers + residual flow head (about 5.3 M parameters, 10-20 MB with fp16 weights) on SyntheticDoc, UVDoc, Book3D spreads and the owner's scanned books (flat pages and textures), on Google Colab within about 90 compute units. The model predicts a correction to the identity map at 1/8 resolution plus a page mask, gutter heat, a bend score and a spread score, so one model serves the whole-frame pass, the page pass and the flat-page gate. Deliverable: one ONNX file with input `image` that lege-gpu loads unchanged, measured with the standalone dewarp tester against the three existing models on 26 hand-held book-spread photos and on a flat-page identity test. Integrating it into the Lege pipeline is a separate follow-up.

### Deferred pipeline memory follow-ups

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.work.pipeline-memory-follow-ups/1`

Two items from the external memory review remain: bring the staged DjVu pipeline under the shared page-memory governor (or carry one reservation per page through its queues; today only its source stage is capped and its queues are not byte-bounded), and measure peak RSS on the decisive workloads (oversized natives, slow writer, one-worker margin, illustration-heavy pages, mid-decode cancel) to size what the review could only identify statically.
